devices.remote_agents_description: Pilot a Récupère agent running on another machine. Install the `recupere-agent` binary on the target, run `sudo recupere-agent init` to generate a token, then `sudo recupere-agent serve`. Default bind is 127.0.0.1:7878 — expose it via `ssh -L 7878:localhost:7878 user@server`, or use a public HTTPS endpoint.

devices.remote_tls_warning_body: The Base URL is not HTTPS and not a loopback address. Bearer token and scan metadata would travel unencrypted. Use `https://` or expose the agent over SSH tunnel to 127.0.0.1.

limitation.deleted_recovery_limited: Deleted-file recovery remains a conservative MVP focused on filesystem-metadata reconstruction.
limitation.scores_estimate_deleted: Recoverability scores remain estimates and do not guarantee a complete reconstruction, especially for fragmented deleted files.
limitation.catalog_only: This build can catalog readable files on mounted volumes, but it does not analyze deleted entries or perform carving.
limitation.scores_estimate_metadata: Recoverability scores are estimates derived from device metadata, not from recovered deleted-file evidence.
limitation.carving_limited: Signature carving currently searches only a small set of known formats (JPEG, PNG, PDF, ZIP) and may miss fragmented or containerized files.
limitation.ext4_mvp: The ext4 deleted-file MVP scans orphaned deleted inodes but does not replay the journal and often cannot recover the original filename.
limitation.hfsplus_mvp: The HFS+ deleted-file MVP scans residual catalog records and can follow data-fork extents-overflow records, but does not replay the journal.
limitation.apfs_mvp: The APFS deleted-file MVP scans only orphaned regular-file inodes. Snapshot-based recovery, encryption-aware recovery, and broader reconstruction are not implemented.
limitation.apfs_snapshot_gap: APFS snapshot- or clone-based recovery is still not delivered in this build. Treat any current APFS result as a conservative present-state or orphan-only view, not as full APFS history traversal.
limitation.apfs_snapshots_present_unavailable: Local APFS snapshots appear to be present on this mounted volume, but snapshot traversal and recovery from that history are not delivered yet in this build.
limitation.lost_volume_conservative: Potential lost-volume detection remains conservative. A candidate does not guarantee the full filesystem can be recovered intact.
limitation.apfs_support_limited: APFS support reconstructs only conservative visible files plus orphaned deleted catalog inodes. Snapshots, encryption, and advanced handling are not implemented.
limitation.apfs_pre_unlock_gap: This APFS/FileVault view is still blocked before unlock. Filesystem-level APFS recovery only becomes meaningful after the original host unlocks the volume with the user's credentials.
limitation.lost_volume_mvp: The lost-volume MVP validates MBR/GPT metadata and scans common aligned boot-sector starts. It is not yet a full-disk signature sweep.
limitation.no_mount: No mounted filesystem path is available for this device, so a live catalog scan cannot be started.
limitation.elevation_required: Raw-device imaging requires administrator approval before the physical source can be read.
limitation.trim_erased: TRIM may already have permanently erased some deleted SSD/NVMe blocks.
limitation.encryption_required: Encrypted content cannot be restored without the original password, key, or unlocked source state.
limitation.encryption_locked_scan_blocked: The current locked view is not treated as a normal filesystem scan surface. Unlock first, or fall back to read-only imaging of the ciphertext only.
limitation.high_risk_image_first: A high-risk device should ideally be imaged once, then analyzed from that image to limit repeated reads.

diagnostic.apfs_operator_subtitle: Clarify what is currently scannable, what stays conservative, and what is still outside this build.
diagnostic.apfs_operator_notice: Current-catalog APFS reads are the safest path in this build. Deleted-file APFS remains limited to orphaned catalog inodes, snapshot history is not delivered yet, and FileVault-style pre-unlock views must be unlocked before expecting filesystem-level recovery.

scan.external_rescue_map_desc: Reuse an existing ddrescue-style rescue map only when you already have the matching local `.partial` image for the destination you are about to pick. Prefix-compatible maps are supported, and sparse/out-of-order maps are also supported when that `.partial` already has the full logical length of the map. The map guides cautious retries; it does not reconstruct missing bytes by itself.
scan.external_rescue_map_hint: Prefix-compatible maps are the simplest case. Sparse or out-of-order layouts are reused only when the local `.partial` already matches the full logical map length; shorter or divergent partial images are rejected.
scan.external_rescue_map_unavailable: A native file picker is required before an external rescue map can be attached in this environment.
scan.external_rescue_map_picker_failed: The rescue map could not be selected.
scan.signature_carving_notice: This MVP first creates a local read-only image, then searches it for JPEG, PNG, PDF, and ZIP signatures. It can now remove up to two neutral gaps conservatively when doing so restores a structurally valid file, but broader multi-fragment carving is still not implemented.
scan.lost_volume_notice: This MVP first creates a local read-only source snapshot, extracts the recovered volume candidate {{label}} as a local slice, then catalogs visible {{filesystem}} files and, when supported, reconstructs deleted entries from that slice. It does not rewrite partition tables or mount the recovered volume automatically.
scan.lost_volume_ready: Ready to analyze {{label}} as a recovered {{filesystem}} candidate.
scan.lost_volume_missing_candidate: The recovered-volume candidate is missing from the current session. Return to Expert mode and select it again.
scan.deleted_ntfs_notice: This NTFS MVP creates a local read-only image, scans deleted MFT records, and reconstructs resident data or non-resident runlists only when their clusters still appear free in the current allocation bitmap. Reused clusters stop reconstruction early.
scan.deleted_fat32_notice: This FAT32 MVP creates a local read-only image, analyzes deleted directory entries, and reconstructs files conservatively. Fragmented files may be incomplete.
scan.deleted_exfat_notice: This exFAT MVP creates a local read-only image, analyzes deleted directory entries, and reconstructs files conservatively from clusters that still appear free in the allocation bitmap. Reused clusters stop reconstruction early.
scan.deleted_ext4_notice: This ext4 MVP creates a local read-only image, scans deleted orphaned inodes, and reconstructs only blocks that still appear free in the current allocation bitmap. Original filenames are usually unavailable, journal replay is not used, and reused blocks stop reconstruction early.
scan.deleted_hfsplus_notice: This HFS+ MVP creates a local read-only image, scans residual catalog records from leaf-node slack, reconstructs data-fork bytes that still map cleanly through inline extents plus conservative extents-overflow follow-up, and now preserves reconstructible resource-fork bytes as raw sidecars during export. Journal replay is not implemented yet.
scan.deleted_apfs_notice: This APFS MVP creates a local read-only image, scans the current catalog metadata for orphaned regular-file inodes that no longer have an active directory record, and reconstructs only extents that remain directly addressable there. Snapshot-based recovery, encryption-aware recovery, and broader deleted APFS reconstruction are not implemented yet.

results.catalog_notice: These results reflect files currently readable on the mounted volume (inventory scan). To recover deleted files, run a filesystem-specific recovery scan or signature carving from the Scan page.
results.carved_notice: These results come from the signature-carving MVP. The app searched the local recovery image for JPEG, PNG, PDF, and ZIP signatures, then reconstructed conservative byte ranges with lightweight format validation when possible. It can now remove up to three neutral gaps across at most four assembled segments when doing so restores a structurally valid file, but broader arbitrary multi-fragment carving is still not implemented. File names are synthetic and carved integrity remains an estimate.
results.lost_volume_notice: These results come from the recovered-volume MVP. The app created a local source snapshot, extracted the candidate {{label}}, then cataloged visible files and, when supported, reconstructed deleted {{filesystem}} entries from that local slice. The candidate remains conservative and is not proof that the full original partition can be mounted intact.
results.deleted_ntfs_notice: These results come from the NTFS deleted-file MVP. Names and timestamps come from deleted MFT metadata, while reconstructible bytes are limited to resident payloads or non-resident runs whose clusters still appear free in the current NTFS bitmap. Named alternate data streams are surfaced when their metadata still remains reconstructible and will export separately as raw sidecars. Once a later cluster has already been reused, the displayed size reflects only the prefix that can still be reconstructed confidently. Integrity remains an estimate.
results.deleted_fat32_notice: These results come from the FAT32 deleted-file MVP. Long names are reconstructed when their directory entries are still present; otherwise the app falls back to short 8.3 aliases. When later clusters have already been reused, the displayed size reflects only the bytes that can still be reconstructed confidently. FAT32 may still expose source creation/modification timestamps, but not a reliable deletion timestamp. Integrity remains an estimate.
results.deleted_exfat_notice: These results come from the exFAT deleted-file MVP. Names and allocation metadata come from deleted directory entries, while reconstructible bytes are limited to clusters that still appear free in the allocation bitmap. Once a later cluster has already been reused, the displayed size reflects only the prefix that can still be reconstructed confidently. Integrity remains an estimate.
results.deleted_ext4_notice: These results come from the ext4 deleted-file MVP. The workflow scans orphaned deleted inodes from a local image and reconstructs only blocks that still appear free in the current bitmap. Original names are usually gone, so filenames may be inferred from content signatures or fall back to inode-based names. Journal-assisted recovery is not implemented yet. Integrity remains an estimate.
results.deleted_hfsplus_notice: These results come from the HFS+ deleted-file MVP. The workflow scans residual catalog records still visible in leaf-node slack from a local image, then reconstructs data-fork bytes that remain directly addressable through inline extents plus conservative extents-overflow follow-up. Resource forks and journal replay are not implemented yet. Integrity remains an estimate.
results.deleted_apfs_notice: These results come from the APFS deleted-file MVP. The workflow scans the current catalog metadata from a local image for orphaned regular-file inodes that no longer have an active directory record, then reconstructs only extents that remain directly addressable there. Snapshot-based recovery, encryption-aware recovery, and broader deleted APFS reconstruction are not implemented yet. Integrity remains an estimate.

export.catalog_notice: This export copies files from an inventory scan (currently readable on the mounted volume). To export deleted files, run a filesystem-specific recovery scan first.
export.carved_notice: This export reconstructs carved files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. When up to three neutral gaps can be removed conservatively to restore a valid structure, the exported payload may contain as many as four stitched byte runs instead of one contiguous range.
export.lost_volume_notice: This export reconstructs files from the local slice extracted out of recovered volume candidate {{label}}, whether they were still visible there or, when supported, recovered as deleted entries. It never writes to the source device and it does not repair the original partition table.
export.deleted_ntfs_notice: This export reconstructs deleted NTFS files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. If named alternate data streams remain reconstructible, they are emitted separately as raw `.ads.<stream>.bin` sidecars. If an NTFS runlist stays only partially reconstructible, only the prefix that can still be rebuilt confidently is exported.
export.deleted_fat32_notice: This export reconstructs deleted FAT32 files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. If the original deleted size cannot be reconstructed confidently, only the recoverable bytes are exported.
export.deleted_exfat_notice: This export reconstructs deleted exFAT files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. If later clusters have already been reallocated, only the prefix that can still be reconstructed confidently is exported.
export.deleted_ext4_notice: This export reconstructs deleted ext4 inode payloads from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. When later blocks have already been reused, only the prefix that still maps to free blocks is exported.
export.deleted_hfsplus_notice: This export reconstructs deleted HFS+ catalog-record files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. Data-fork extents that remain directly addressable through inline records plus conservative extents-overflow follow-up are exported as the main file, and reconstructible resource-fork bytes are emitted separately as raw `.resource-fork.bin` sidecars.
export.resource_fork_notice: {{count}} selected file(s) include a reconstructible HFS+ resource fork. Export will write those bytes as raw `.resource-fork.bin` sidecars ({{bytes}} total), not as a full AppleDouble/Finder metadata recreation.
export.ads_notice: {{count}} NTFS alternate data stream(s) remain reconstructible in the current selection. Export will write those bytes as raw `.ads.<stream>.bin` sidecars ({{bytes}} total), not as native NTFS ADS recreation.
export.snapshot_notice: {{count}} selected file(s) depend on snapshot-derived metadata. Preview and verify those exports locally because live state may have diverged since that snapshot.
export.journal_notice: {{count}} selected file(s) depend on journal-derived metadata. Treat them as higher-risk and confirm previews before trusting the exported bytes.
export.apfs_operator_notice: APFS export provenance matters: current-catalog files are usually the safest, while snapshot- and journal-derived files deserve extra local preview and post-export verification.
export.apfs_reassembled_notice: {{count}} APFS current-catalog deleted file(s) in this export are qualified as reassembled. They are more actionable than preview-first candidates, but still deserve preview and post-export verification because structural validation is not available yet.
export.apfs_preview_first_default_notice: {{count}} APFS catalog-derived deleted file(s) were held out of the default export batch because structural validation is still unavailable. Preview and select them explicitly from Results if you want to export them anyway.
export.compressed_notice: {{count}} selected file(s) include compressed payload reconstruction. Export remains read-only and local, but preview verification is recommended before relying on the output.
export.high_complexity_notice: {{count}} selected file(s) were reconstructed through higher-complexity assembly or metadata paths. Export only to a safe destination and verify the output before replacing originals.
export.deleted_apfs_notice: This export reconstructs deleted APFS orphaned-inode files from the local recovery image, never from a writeable source path. Only extents that remain directly addressable in the current catalog metadata state are exported; snapshot-based recovery and broader APFS deleted reconstruction are not included in this MVP.

metadata_only.title: Metadata-first assessment
metadata_only.description_with_deleted: This build can catalog readable files on mounted volumes, run a conservative deleted-entry recovery workflow, and carve a small set of known signatures from a local image.
metadata_only.description_with_carving: This build can catalog readable files on mounted volumes and carve a small set of known signatures from a local image, but filesystem-specific deleted entries remain limited.
metadata_only.description_basic: This build can catalog readable files on mounted volumes, but deleted entries and carved blocks are not analyzed yet.

trim.title: TRIM is enabled
trim.description: Deleted blocks on SSD/NVMe media may already have been reclaimed by the controller.

encryption.title: Encryption detected
encryption.description: Recovered content remains limited without the original unlock credential or key material.

health.title: Device health is poor
health.description: Repeated reads may worsen access to unstable sectors on a failing device.

degraded.title: Device status is degraded
degraded.description: The medium remains readable, but the detected health indicators are not fully healthy.

unknown_fs.title: Unknown filesystem
unknown_fs.description: The current read-only detector could not map the filesystem to a supported analyzer.

potential_lost_volume.title: Potential lost volume metadata detected
potential_lost_volume.description: Plausible partition-table entries or filesystem boot signatures were found on the raw source. Treat them as conservative candidates until a dedicated recovery workflow validates them further.

stop_usage.title: Stop non-essential use
stop_usage.description: Avoid new writes or repeated retries on the source device until a safer imaging workflow is available.

image_first.title: Create a read-only disk image first
image_first.description_encrypted: This source still appears locked by encryption. Image the raw ciphertext if needed, but unlock on the original host before expecting filesystem-level recovery.
image_first.description_blocked: This host cannot start raw read-only imaging for this source yet.
image_first.description_elevation: Raw read-only imaging remains available for this source, but macOS will request administrator approval before reading the physical device.
image_first.description_with_deleted: Create a standalone local read-only image before deeper analysis, or let the deleted-file workflow create one automatically.
image_first.description_default: Create a standalone local read-only image before deeper analysis to limit repeated reads on fragile media.

scan_signature_carving.title: Run signature carving from a local image
scan_signature_carving.description: This MVP images the source read-only, then searches the local image for JPEG, PNG, PDF, and ZIP signatures. Fragmented files may be missing or incomplete.

scan_lost_volume.title: Analyze the recovered volume candidate
scan_lost_volume.description_multiple: Several potential volumes were detected. Create a local read-only snapshot and isolate the best candidate for analysis.
scan_lost_volume.description_single: Create a local read-only snapshot, isolate the candidate volume, then analyze its filesystem.

review_potential_volumes.title: Inspect potential lost volumes
review_potential_volumes.description_apfs: Review the offsets, APFS container hints, and confidence levels for raw-source volume candidates before deciding whether to image or continue with filesystem-specific recovery.

caution.apfs_reassembled_verify: APFS deleted results qualified as reassembled are stronger than preview-first leads, but they still rely on catalog evidence and should be previewed and checked after export.
caution.compressed_batches: Compressed payloads depend on successful decompression and should be exported in small validated batches.
caution.truncated_payload: Some files expose an expected size larger than the reconstructible payload. Exported bytes may only represent a trusted prefix.

hardware_errors.disk_unreadable_title: The disk stops responding during reads
hardware_errors.disk_unreadable_body: This usually means hardware failure (head crash, bad sectors spreading, connection problem). Stop the current scan. Power the disk off, plug it into a different cable and port if possible, and try again. If it still fails, imaging with cautious mode (skip unreadable ranges) is the only safe move — every read attempt on failing hardware reduces the chance of getting anything out.
hardware_errors.disk_unreadable_advice: Safer next step: switch to Imaging → Cautious mode.
hardware_errors.insufficient_space_body: Récupère needs free space at least equal to the recovered-file set. Pick another destination (external drive, different partition) and resume the export — nothing on the source is lost.
hardware_errors.insufficient_space_advice: Safer next step: choose a destination with at least {{needed}} free.
hardware_errors.permission_denied_title: The system refused to open the device
hardware_errors.permission_denied_body: Raw-disk access needs elevated privileges on every OS. On macOS this is Full Disk Access; on Linux this is root or a udev rule; on Windows this is Administrator + an unlocked volume. The file it tried to open is: {{path}}.
hardware_errors.permission_denied_advice: Safer next step: close Récupère, re-launch it with elevated privileges, and retry.
hardware_errors.usb_disconnect_body: A USB/Thunderbolt drive unplugged (or went into sleep). Partial results are kept — you can resume from the point where Récupère stopped. If this keeps happening, the cable or the enclosure is often the culprit; try a different one before blaming the disk.
hardware_errors.usb_disconnect_advice: Safer next step: re-plug the disk, then click Resume.
hardware_errors.raw_unmounted_title: The disk is visible but not mounted
hardware_errors.raw_unmounted_body: The OS sees a block device but didn't assign a mount point — typical when a partition table is wiped, a RAID member is on its own, or an encrypted volume hasn't been unlocked. Récupère lists it under 'Unmounted devices' so you can image it first and then analyse the copy.
hardware_errors.raw_unmounted_advice: Safer next step: image the device read-only before any recovery attempt.
hardware_errors.encrypted_locked_body: The volume appears to be {{encryption_type}}. We can image the raw ciphertext, but we can't read the filesystem until it's unlocked on the original host OS with the user's passphrase. Once unlocked, re-run the scan against the unlocked mount point.
hardware_errors.encrypted_locked_advice: Safer next step: unlock on the original host, then re-scan.
hardware_errors.smart_warning_title: SMART flags this disk as unhealthy
hardware_errors.smart_warning_body: SMART counters (reallocated / pending / uncorrectable sectors) went past the healthy threshold. The disk is still usable for read-only imaging but should not be written to. Plan a replacement soon even if you recover everything you need.
hardware_errors.smart_warning_advice: Safer next step: finish imaging now, replace hardware afterwards.
